heard: Think the moon doesn't spin, that is a total myth. Our moon actually rotates on its axis at the exact same speed it orbits Earth. This synchronous tidal locking is caused by Earth's gravity stretching the lunar body into physical bulges. Gravity pulls on these bulges like a brake, forcing the spin to match the orbit. This constant friction slows the rotation and pushes the moon away by four centimeters every year. We finally saw the far side when the Soviet Luna 3 photographed it in 1959. Even Pluto and its moon, Charon, are mutually caught in the same gravitational grip. This synchronization hides the far side forever, which is why people still believe the moon doesn't spin.
